about: Ranking rules for the review-queue pages (queue/build.py). A pull request's tier is the lowest tier number any of its changed files falls in; within a tier the needs-a-review track orders by age at the current head (oldest first) and then by size (smallest first). Change a rule by pull request; the page shows, per row, the rule lines that placed it.

tracks.needs_review: open, not a draft, title not marked WIP, mergeable state not dirty (see needs_rebase), head pushed within stale_days, no review by anyone but the author at the current head, and no peeryard review at that head (or carried to it: see peeryard_review); ordered by tier, then by days at the current head (longest waiting first), then by size
tracks.needs_maintainer: open, not a draft, at least one review at the current head (a peeryard review counts, carried or not), CI green or absent, mergeable state clean (or not yet computed by GitHub, which recomputes lazily after the base branch moves; asked again before judging, and shown as such); ordered by days since the last activity
tracks.carried: open upstream pull requests this tree carries as patches (patches/*/patches.json with an upstream_pr and a status that is not candidate, withdrawn or merged-in-<tag>), ordered by how many examples need them; one GitHub reports merged (into a branch not yet in the release the rig uses) is listed apart as merged into its base and carried until release, not as needing a maintainer
tracks.stale: open pull requests whose head is older than stale_days: listed at the end, unranked, so the work list stays a work list
tracks.same_change: open pull requests, drafts included, whose production diff (src/main and */src/main, from the merge base with their base branch to the head, changed lines only: git diff -U0) has the same git patch-id --stable, so one change made on two bases still matches: one group, earliest opened first, the others marked as the same production change as it; the author is not a factor (two open copies of one change are one review), and tests, docs and base branch may differ
tracks.same_issue: open pull requests, drafts included, by different authors (one author's pull requests on one issue are usually parts of a series), that say they address the same issue (#N or a link: in the title, after a lead word in the description such as fixes, closes, addresses, refs or part of, or opening the description; a number the description only cites for context does not count; GitHub says N is an issue, not a pull request) and change at least one of the same production files; a pair already in one same-change group is not repeated, and a pull request from a release branch (same_change.release_head) is left out, since it lists every pull request in the release
tracks.peeryard_review: a pull-request review or issue comment that carries the structured marker <!-- peeryard {...} --> (queue/mark.py: head, base, kind, prod_patch_id), or the credit-line words 'using peeryard' / 'using forkbench', or (backfill, bounded by queue/reviewers.json) a credit-line opening by a listed login before the listed date; the latest such post after the head commit is the review shown. A post made at an earlier head is carried when the production patch-id (git diff -U0 over src/main and */src/main from the merge base, git patch-id --stable) at that head equals the current one: a rebase or a tests-only push keeps the review, a production change returns the pull request to the needs-a-review track
tracks.needs_rebase: open, not a draft, not WIP, head pushed within stale_days, no review at the current head, and GitHub's mergeable state is dirty (conflicts with the base branch): an author action before anything else, so not offered for review by default, though still reviewable on its own merge base; read from GitHub, nothing is posted (the maintainers asked for no notification-only comments), and the row clears when the author rebases; ordered by tier, then days at the current head
tracks.coverage: the line at the top of the index: live pull requests (head within stale_days, not WIP), how many have a review at head by anyone, how many a peeryard review and of which kinds (the marker's kind; a post without a marker is 'executed' when its report carries an Executed: line or an (executed) tag, else 'read'), how many need a review or a rebase, tier-1 live vs tier-1 with an executed peeryard review, live claims, and the outcome counts; the same numbers go into history/<date>.json (coverage, outcomes) so a burn-down can be read
tracks.outcomes: closed pull requests that had a peeryard review (found by 'using peeryard' or the marker in comments, and by the reviewers.json logins as reviewer or commenter for the backfill): merged; 'closed as recommended' when the last review's Recommended: line begins with close, withdraw or drop; else closed; one row per pull request, latest closed first, on outcomes/
tracks.claims: queue/claims.json, edited by queue/claim.py and committed: a claim (pr, by, kind, expires_at; 24 h by default) tags the row on the page and is skipped by queue/next.py when it is someone else's; it never hides a pull request and nothing is posted to GitHub; expired claims are ignored
tracks.next: queue/next.py: the needs-a-review track in rank order, minus others' claims, filled to a time budget with a rule-based estimate per item (RULES in the script: read-review 20/45/90 min by size under 80/400 changed lines; a tier-1 or tier-2 production change that also changes tests adds a 25 min revert-check; tests-only is a revert-check; docs a read; a same-change or same-issue group adds a compare over the set); prints the kinds, the estimate, the rule lines, and the claim and mark commands

not_a_factor: the author (every pull request is scored the same way, peeryard's own included)
